newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-StanChart wins and loses on Forex.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-StanChart wins and loses on Forex.

text.p: Standard Chartered Plc, the London-based bank with a big Asia-Pacific region franchise, on Wednesday reported first-half, pre-tax profits of 435 million pounds ($707 million), seriously affected by the strength of sterling.

The figure compared to 448 million pounds last year but that included an exceptional gain of 46 million pounds while trading profit was up eight percent but would have risen 16 percent if exchange rates had remained constant.
At the same time, StanChart reported big profits from foreign exchange trading in the Far East where currency turmoil has been particularly strong in recent months.
Chief Executive Malcolm Williamson told Reuters the bank had not experienced such a big effect on its profits from translation into sterling before.

"The problem we have...is that we are very much a dollar-related bank, we either get our money in US dollars or currencies that are linked to it or currencies that have depreciated even more against sterling over the last year," Williamson said.
At constant exchange rates, the bank's trading profit rose by 16 percent but was only up a reported eight percent to 434 million pounds compared to 402 million pounds in the first half of 1996.
The bank used a sterling/dollar rate of 1.67 for the first half of this year, compared to 1.55 this time last year.
Williamson calculated that a rough rule of thumb is that StanChart loses around 50 million pounds on reported profit figures for every one percent change in the exchange rate.
But he pointed out that this was a rough calculation because the figures are affected both on the costs and income side and in the latter are affected by the mix of assets on the balance sheet.

On the other hand, income from foreign exchange rose sharply to 108 million pounds in the first half from 80 million pounds in the same period last year, helping raise the bank's Treasury profits to 103 million pounds from 76 million last time.
Williamson dismissed as "absolutely untrue" recent rumours in the foreign exchange markets that Standard Chartered had lost money in the volatility.
"We've had a very good record on this in the last few months," Williamson said. "You get daily ups and downs, but we've managed our book tightly and well and it's continued through July."
He said the financial turmoil in Thailand, Indonesia and Philippines had not affected the bank's other business unduly.

While StanChart's exposure to the Thai property sector was nil on a direct basis, Williamson said the bank had some counterparty exposure to Thai banks and finance houses and has made a special provision of five million pounds as a precaution.

"If you're big in a country, it's hard not to have some exposure, Williamson said. "Even though you yourself can keep your hands clean, the risk is that you get caught with some counterparty exposure with people who have been more profligate."

StanChart said it raised its interim dividend by 24 percent to 5.25 pence per share from 4.25 pence for the first half of last year. Both dividend and pre-tax profit figures were within market expectations.
Of Standard Chartered's trading profit, 156 million pounds, or 36 percent, comes from Hong Kong and the bank said it was optimistic about the development of the Hong Kong economy.
Standard Chartered said price competition for new lending in the Far East had been severe and saw its net interest margin edge lower to 3.4 percent from 3.5 percent.
Williamson said the bank had countered margin pressure in Hong Kong by going for growth in volumes and said that its business in Malaysia was also doing well.
Costs in the bank were higher, as it had flagged earlier, but income rose to a greater degree, leaving the cost to income ratio at 53.7 percent compared to 55.7 percent at the end of last year.
"The rise in costs is a question of putting resource where we really see the future," Williamson said.
On the income side, the biggest rise came from the Treasury operations but personal banking also produced good figures, increasing pre-provision profit by 16 percent.
StanChart shares were higher after the figures were announced, standing 32 pence firmer at 1037.5p after reaching an earlier high of 1042p.
